p: You'll find it on the Broad Street side of the city centre, which puts it in a cracking spot for a walk-round afterwards. Brindleyplace and the canal towpaths are close by, and the National SEA LIFE Centre Birmingham sits by the water there too, so a bricks-then-fishes double header is easy to pull off if the kids still have energy to burn.

A couple of practical bits help the day go smoothly. Little ones will be down on the floor building, crawling and climbing, so comfy clothes beat Sunday best, and socks are a good idea for any soft play. A bottle of water and a snack in the bag never hurts with tired builders. Prams and buggies can be awkward in busy indoor spaces, so if your youngest can manage on foot or in a sling, life gets easier.

For a calmer visit, aim for the first sessions of the day or term-time weekdays, when there's more room around the build tables. Have a quick chat with the kids beforehand about which bits they're most excited for, as it saves a stampede in five directions at once. And leave a bit of time for the shop on the way out, because somebody will definitely be asking.
